keys.lpn_status_hidden_tip: Show the hidden message on the map again.
keys.lpn_wrong_tip: Report an error on this page. This opens a box to choose the problem, add a comment, and enter an email address if a reply is wanted. All fields are optional, and nothing is sent until you press Send.
keys.lpn_wrong_thanks: Thank you. Your report was received.
keys.lpn_fb_intro: Canned messages (optional). Nothing is sent until you press Send.
keys.lpn_fb_pick_wording: The wording or translation is wrong
keys.lpn_fb_email: Email (optional, only if you want a reply)
keys.lpn_fb_sends: What this sends: the name of this page, your language, the version of the site, the code of the message on the map if there is one, and what you chose or typed. Never your drawing or your network. Your email address is used only to reply to you.
keys.lpn_fb_failed: That did not reach us. What you wrote is still here, so you can try again.
keys.lpn_fb_bad_email: That email address does not look right. Correct it, or leave it empty.
keys.lpn_fb_busy: Too many messages have arrived in the last few minutes. What you wrote is still here, so you can try again later.
keys.lpn_status_example_opened: Opened {name} as a copy. Save it with File, Save as.
keys.lpn_map_unmeasurable: This page could not determine the size of the drawing area, so the map shows the last view it was able to compute. Resizing the window repeats the measurement. If this persists, the usual cause is a browser extension that blocks page measurements.
keys.lpn_ex_basic_si_desc: Two reservoirs, a pump, and a small loop. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.
keys.lpn_ex_basic_us_desc: Two reservoirs, a pump, and a small loop. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.
keys.lpn_ex_net1_title: EPANET Net1 plus rule-based controls, gpm (US)
keys.lpn_ex_net1_desc: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. A fictional EPANET example with chlorine, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 1 pump, and two rule-based controls.
keys.lpn_ex_net1_si_title: EPANET Net1 plus rule-based controls, L/s (SI)
keys.lpn_ex_net1_si_desc: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. A fictional EPANET example converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with chlorine, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 1 pump, and two rule-based controls.
keys.lpn_ex_net1_scn_desc: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. EPANET's Net1 with four scenarios under Base, the average day: Max day (demand multiplier 1.5) and Peak hour (2.25), each with a main break child, and the two children share one alternative. To test fire flow, make Max day current, select junction 23, choose Water, Analyze, Fire flow analysis, and enter a Required fire flow of 1,500 gpm.
keys.lpn_ex_valves_desc: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. A hilltop reservoir feeds a hub through a PBV, with a PRV, PSV, FCV, TCV, and GPV branching off it, each one controlling at the solved state.
keys.lpn_ex_net2_si_desc: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. An EPANET example at Branford, Connecticut, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches: 35 junctions and 1 tank, with no reservoir, no pump, and no valves, about 2 km by 4 km. Fluoride, a non-reactive substance, enters at one source.
keys.lpn_ex_net2_desc: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. An EPANET example at Branford, Connecticut: 35 junctions and 1 tank, with no reservoir, no pump, and no valves, about 1 mile by 2 miles. Fluoride, a non-reactive substance, enters at one source.
keys.lpn_ex_net3_si_desc: Liters per second, with meters and millimeters. An EPANET example at Novato, California, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with the world map behind it: 92 junctions, 3 tanks, and 2 reservoirs, no valves, about 8 km square. A 24-hour extended-period simulation, with a source trace from the Lake.
keys.lpn_ex_net3_desc: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. An EPANET example at Novato, California, with the world map behind it: 92 junctions, 3 tanks, and 2 reservoirs, no valves, about 5 miles square. A 24-hour extended-period simulation, with a source trace from the Lake.
keys.lpn_ex_elm_street_desc: Gallons per minute, with feet and inches. Prescott Valley, Arizona: 17 junctions, 1 reservoir, and 1 pump. A commercial site solved for fire flow on top of maximum day demand, at one moment in time, drawn over a site plan.
keys.lpn_confirm_example: This adds the example to the network you already have. Continue?
keys.lpn_demand_tip: Flows taken out of the network at this node. Enter a negative number for flow put into the network here.
keys.lpn_units_warn_title: This unit defines how your inputs are read
keys.lpn_units_warn_lead: {unit} is the unit of what you enter for:
keys.lpn_units_nondestructive_desc: Non-destructive: leaves every input as it is and reinterprets it in the new unit.
keys.lpn_units_destructive_desc: Destructive: rewrites every input with a mathematical conversion, so the network stays physically close to the same, within conversion tolerances. It loses the original inputs. Undo puts them back.
keys.lpn_status_reinterpreted: Values ({n}) now mean {unit}. Nothing was rewritten.
keys.lpn_result_gradient_tip: Head loss divided by the length of the pipe. Use it to compare pipes of different lengths against one design limit.
keys.lpn_result_water_age_tip: Time the water reaching this point has spent in the system. Where flows meet, the number is the average of the arriving ages, weighted by flow. In a tank it is the average age of the water held, so a tank that turns over slowly usually holds the oldest water in a network. There is no regulatory limit to compare it against, so evaluate it against conditions in the system being modeled.
keys.lpn_result_source_share_tip: Share of the water reaching this point that came from the trace node. This is what the Source trace analysis reports.
keys.lpn_result_head_tip: Potential energy of the water at this node, written as a height of water column. It is an absolute height, where pressure is a gauge measurement.
keys.lpn_result_depth_tip: Depth of water in the tank at the time shown, measured up from the tank bottom: the head minus the tank elevation.
keys.lpn_result_tank_volume_tip: Volume of water above the lowest water depth, so it is zero at that depth. The EPANET tank volume also includes the water below the lowest water depth, which still counts toward mixing and water age, so the tank elevation stays at the tank bottom.
keys.lpn_settings_restore_tip: Reset the settings of this project only. The drawing and other projects are not changed. To reuse a set of settings, save a project file that contains only settings.
keys.lpn_reset_all_tip: Delete every project, every background image, every setting, and your unit choices, then reload the page exactly as a first-time visitor sees it. This is the only reset that clears everything.
keys.lpn_v2_restore_confirm: This calculator stores project units and inputs as entered, but it formerly converted numbers to SI for storage. This project was saved before that change, so its numbers were stored in SI. Convert them one last time to the current units? To help you judge, here are some diameters that would be converted, with their values before and after:
keys.lpn_v2_restore_no: Close so that I can check the current units first
keys.lpn_storage_too_new: This project was saved by a newer version of the page, so it cannot be opened here.
keys.lpn_convas_coordsys_tip: The coordinate system the copy is converted to. When it differs from that of this project, two placement steps follow. For a project that is already georeferenced, both steps open completed, ready to accept or change.
keys.lpn_convas_epsg_tip: Choose a coordinate system from the EPSG register. WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), latitude and longitude, is the suggested choice. WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator (EPSG:3857), commonly called Web Mercator, gives x and y in meters, and its map distances exceed ground distances away from the equator. Pipe lengths are computed as ground distances in either system.
keys.lpn_convas_unnamed_tip: Local coordinates in the length unit, with the world map attached.
keys.lpn_convas_none_tip: Local coordinates in the length unit, with no world map for now.
keys.lpn_convas_units_tip: The units the copy is converted to.
keys.lpn_convas_round_tip: The step to round to, applied only to the numbers this conversion rewrites. Values whose unit does not change are left as they are.
keys.lpn_convas_label_tip: Text added after this value on the copy's map labels, such as ' mm' or ' gpm'. Pre-filled from the unit chosen above; clear it for no suffix.
keys.lpn_convas_oneway: Converting back is a second conversion, not an undo. A number converted and converted back may not return exactly as it was entered.
keys.lpn_convas_no_transform: {crs} is one of the few listed coordinate systems without usable projection information, so it cannot be converted to or from. Nothing was converted.
keys.lpn_convas_done: The converted copy is {name}. The original project is unchanged.
keys.lpn_convas_cancelled: Nothing was converted. The copy is closed, and the original project is unchanged.
keys.lpn_file_convert_as_tip: Copy this project to a new tab and convert the copy to the coordinate system and units you choose. When the coordinate system changes, a wizard guides you through zooming the map behind your network approximately, then scaling and rotating your network on the map more closely. This project is left exactly as it is. To georeference without converting anything, use Map, World map, Attach instead.
keys.lpn_georef_answered: This project is already georeferenced, so the network is already on the map and nothing has been moved. Check that it is in the right place, then press the Put the model here button and the Keep this placement button.
keys.lpn_georef_intro: Placing the model takes two steps. Step 1 is approximate: the model stays fixed on the screen while you pan and zoom the map behind it, until the site is under the model at about the right scale. This step has no rotation. Step 2 is precise: drag, resize, and rotate the model itself. The project starts on a map of the whole world, so find the location first, then press the Put the model here button.
keys.lpn_georef_adjust: The model is now attached to the map, so it moves with the map. Drag the model to move it, drag a corner to resize it, or drag the round handle above the model to rotate it. Or enter the ground distance and the rotation angle below.
keys.lpn_georef_step1_hint: The project stays fixed on the screen. Pan and zoom the map underneath it until the map shows approximately the right location at approximately the right scale, then press the Put the model here button.
keys.lpn_georef_size_prompt: About how wide is the site, across the whole project?
keys.lpn_tool_add_chain_tip: Chain junctions and pipes: specify a point on the map to add a junction, then specify each next point to add a pipe and a junction. Specify an existing node to continue from it. Press Escape to end the chain.
keys.lpn_tool_add_shape_tip: Draw a point, a polyline, or a polygon on the map. A Shape is annotation and is not part of the network. Specify each point, then specify the last point again, press Enter, or right-click to finish. Specify the first point again to close the Shape into a polygon.
keys.lpn_tool_vertices_tip: Add and remove pipe vertices. Specify a point on a pipe to add a vertex, select a vertex to remove it, and drag a vertex to move it. A vertex changes automatic length, but doesn’t add or change minor (local) losses.
keys.lpn_tool_zoom_extent_tip: Fit the whole network to the map window. To zoom to a rectangle you drag instead, press W or click the small triangle in the corner of the Zoom to fit toolbar button. See also the zoom controls at the upper right of the map.
keys.lpn_tool_zoom_selection_tip: Fit the selected assets to the map window. Select one or more assets first.
keys.lpn_tool_zoom_window_tip: Specify corners or drag a rectangle. Press again for Zoom to fit.
keys.lpn_find_menu_tip: Simple or complex find and replace
keys.lpn_color_legend_open_tip: Press to open the coloring settings and change these colors.
keys.lpn_color_ranges_note: The boundaries below are fixed once set; they do not follow the results as they change. Choosing a data classification method above sets the boundaries from the current state of the system. If you change any value by hand, the method above becomes Manual.
keys.lpn_color_criterion_note: This method takes its boundaries from a design standard, so the number of colors is fixed while this method is chosen.
keys.lpn_color_break_number: A boundary must be a number. The map is unchanged.
keys.lpn_color_break_order: Each boundary must be larger than the one before it. The map is unchanged.
keys.lpn_color_break_count: There must be one boundary fewer than the number of colors. The map is unchanged.
keys.lpn_georef_scale_tip: Calculated automatically. Edit to change. Enter 1 to use the file coordinates unchanged as ground distance, for example for a file with no coordinate system.
keys.lpn_georef_rotation_tip: Counterclockwise rotation of the whole model, to align it with the new coordinate system.
keys.lpn_georef_confirm: Place the model here permanently? Assets can still be dragged one at a time afterwards, but proceeding now converts all the coordinates at once. To get the old coordinates back, return to the original project and close this one without saving.
keys.lpn_georef_done: This project is now on the new coordinate system. You may continue to drag any assets that need further adjustment.
keys.lpn_georef_backdrop_unrotated: The background image was moved and resized with the model, but it could not be rotated. Use Map, Background image, Move to align it.
keys.lpn_georef_empty: That file has no network in it, so there is nothing to place.
keys.lpn_georef_unavailable: The placement tool did not load. Reload the page and try again.
keys.lpn_georef_tab_locked: Finish the conversion with the "Keep this placement" button, or press Cancel, before you switch projects. The placement applies only to this project.
keys.lpn_georef_save_locked: Finish the conversion with the "Keep this placement" button, or press Cancel, before you save. The project is still being placed, so what is on the screen is not yet what would be written to the file.
keys.lpn_goto_menu: Go to a latitude and longitude…
keys.lpn_goto_prompt: Latitude and longitude, in that order, separated by a comma or a space
keys.lpn_goto_bad: Can't read coordinates. Try again. Examples: 38,-122 or 38.122 or 38 -122
keys.lpn_georef_twopt_tip: Place the model exactly when the true latitude and longitude of two points on the drawing are known. Specify one of them, enter its latitude and longitude, then do the same for a second point. The position, scale, and rotation are computed from those two points. Press again to cancel, or press Esc.
keys.lpn_georef_twopt_pick1: Specify a point on your drawing whose latitude and longitude you know.
keys.lpn_georef_twopt_pick2: Now specify a second known point, as far from the first one as you can.
keys.lpn_georef_twopt_same: That is the point you picked first. Pick a different one.
keys.lpn_georef_twopt_done: The model is now placed on the two points entered. Check it, then press the Keep this placement button.
keys.lpn_pane_toggle_tip: Show or hide the panel below the map. It holds graphs and a table for each kind of asset.
keys.lpn_pane_resize: Drag to make the panel taller or shorter
keys.lpn_pane_tab_tip: Edit assets as a spreadsheet-like table. Result columns cannot be edited. See Help, Notes for keyboard shortcuts.
keys.lpn_pane_none: This network has none of these yet.
keys.lpn_pane_filter_none: Nothing in this table matches the filter.
keys.lpn_pane_filter_sel_and: Filtered by {q} and selection only. Showing {n} of {all}.
keys.lpn_pane_filter_sel_none: None of the selected elements are in this table.
keys.lpn_pane_sel_only_none: No elements are selected. Select elements on the map first.
keys.lpn_ovm_child_tip: Child scenarios override this value ({n} total). Click to clear their overrides.
keys.lpn_ovm_dot_set: Inherited. Click to make it an override in this scenario, holding the value shown.
keys.lpn_export_table_scn_note: Results are exported only for the scenario last calculated.
keys.lpn_menu_project_tip: Everything specific to water network modeling (except the animation play controls)
keys.lpn_morph_tip: Change the selected nodes into junctions, reservoirs, or tanks, or the selected links into pipes, pumps, or valves. Each keeps its ID, its location, its connections, and every value the new type also has. In Base the asset itself is changed, and you are asked first if any value would be lost. In any other scenario the new type is an override in that scenario only, and the values only the new type has start from Settings > New assets.
keys.lpn_morph_other_kind: A node can be morphed only into another type of node, and a link only into another type of link. Not morphed: {ids}
keys.lpn_field_type_tip: The type of this asset in this scenario, set by Morph. Clear the override to use the parent scenario's type.
keys.lpn_change_type_key: Each line: ID: the property and value that would be lost
keys.lpn_change_type_surface: These keep the water surface where it was. A reservoir's head is the tank's elevation plus its water depth, and a tank's water depth is the reservoir's head minus its elevation:
keys.lpn_change_type_meaning: These controls and rules test a node being changed, and will read it differently: a junction is tested by its pressure, and a tank or reservoir by its water level.
keys.lpn_change_type_born: These values are new, set as on a newly drawn asset:
keys.lpn_change_type_no_curve: {id}: No pump head curve, so the pump adds no head until one is chosen, and an .inp export writes it as a pipe
keys.lpn_change_type_customers: Only a pipe serves customers, so these customers are connected instead to the node shown in parentheses, where their demand is already applied. They stay where they are drawn, and their demand is unchanged:
keys.lpn_change_type_setting: These controls and rules give or test the setting of a link being changed. A setting is a different quantity on a pipe, a pump, and a valve, so these will read it differently:
keys.lpn_change_type_rules: These rule lines name a link by its kind, and will name its new kind instead:
keys.lpn_tables_menu_tip: View and edit assets in tables in bottom panel.
keys.lpn_run_menu_tip: Run simulation. Unnecessary when "Recalculate automatically" is on in Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics. When Recalculate is off, a toolbar Calculate button appears.
keys.lpn_settings_auto_run_tip: Turn off if recalculation is too slow. While this is on, the Calculate button is hidden.
keys.lpn_time_run_slow: This network took {secs} s to calculate, and it is set to recalculate after every change. To stop that and get a Calculate button back, turn off “Recalculate automatically” in Settings, under Calculation, Hydraulics.
keys.lpn_time_no_report: There is no run report yet. The report is the EPANET text report, so it appears after this network has been calculated.
keys.lpn_confirm_delete_network: Delete every node, pipe, and text label in this project? The background image, the project name, and your settings are kept.
keys.lpn_copy_props_done_ov: Copied the overrides of {id} in this scenario.
keys.lpn_paste_props_off_none: Nothing is copied. Right-click or long press an asset and choose Copy properties.
keys.lpn_paste_props_off_select: Select the assets to paste to, then choose Paste properties to selection.
keys.lpn_paste_props_off_kind: No selected asset can take the copied properties.
keys.lpn_ctx_reset_position_off_tip: Only a label or an attached Text that has been dragged from its own position can be reset.
keys.lpn_tsb_off_tip: Needs extended period results. Set a Total run time in Settings, Calculation, Time, and calculate.
keys.lpn_tsb_max: Close a graph before opening another. Up to {n} stay open.
keys.lpn_paste_done_one: Pasted properties of {id} to {to}. Values changed: {n}.
keys.lpn_paste_done_many: Pasted properties of {id} to {m} assets. Values changed: {n}.
keys.lpn_paste_skip_breakdown: Not pasted: {n} (demand is a list of categories).
keys.lpn_find_source_no_chemical: No chemical is being tracked, so no node has a source.
keys.lpn_find_filter_tip: Show only the rows that match "What to search" above, in each table searched.
keys.lpn_find_filter_none: This query doesn't apply to any table.
keys.lpn_find_count: {n} found. Select one to go to it.
keys.lpn_find_shift_hint: Shift+click to toggle, adding if not in the selection set or removing if already in the selection set.
keys.lpn_find_op_conn_nolinksource: no link path to a source
keys.lpn_find_op_conn_noopensource: no open path to a source
keys.lpn_find_conn_no_fixed: This network has no reservoir or tank, so there is no source to reach. Only no links at node and no open links at node can be searched.
keys.lpn_find_query_tip: The given search as a text query. Changing the query updates the controls above.
keys.lpn_find_query_hint: Combine conditions with AND, OR and ()
keys.lpn_find_q_aside: The controls cannot express the query below, so they are hidden.
keys.lpn_replace_q_bad: This query cannot be understood, so nothing can be changed. Fix it above first.
keys.lpn_find_q_err_empty: The query is empty, so nothing will be searched.
keys.lpn_find_q_err_scope: There is nothing called {w} to search. Try one of: {list}
keys.lpn_find_q_err_dot: Put a dot between what to search and its property, like Junction.ID
keys.lpn_find_q_err_prop: Not a property of {scope}: {w}. Try one of: {list}
keys.lpn_find_q_err_op: Not a condition for {prop}: {w}. Try one of: {list}
keys.lpn_find_q_err_value: This condition needs a value after it: {op}
keys.lpn_find_q_err_quote: Put quotes around a text value: {w} is not a number.
keys.lpn_find_q_err_quote_end: This quoted text has no closing quote.
keys.lpn_find_q_err_close: This parenthesis ( was opened and never closed.
keys.lpn_find_q_err_end: Nothing was expected after this. Join two searches with {and} or {or}.
keys.lpn_replace_asked: Elevations requested for nodes ({n}). Results appear when they are received.
keys.lpn_replace_done: Assets changed: {n}. This can be undone in one step.
keys.lpn_replace_scope: Choose one kind of asset above to change values on.
keys.lpn_profile_draw_start: Select the node where the path starts.
keys.lpn_profile_draw_more: Move over the map to see the path. Select a node to add it. Double-click to finish. Esc cancels.
keys.lpn_profile_draw_blocked: No route from {a} to {b}. Select a different start or end node.
keys.lpn_profile_tap_start: Select the node where the path starts.
keys.lpn_profile_tap_more: Select a node to see the path. Press and hold to add it. Double-tap to finish. Press Profile again to cancel.
keys.lpn_profile_say_idle: Press Profile again to select a new path on the map.
keys.lpn_profile_none: No path yet. Press Profile again to select one on the map.
keys.lpn_profile_choose: Select a start node and an end node.
keys.lpn_profile_no_path: These two nodes are not connected by any route.
keys.lpn_profile_no_solve: No results yet, so only the ground line is drawn.
keys.lpn_profile_edit_tip: Change one end of the path, or take one node off it, without drawing the whole path again.
keys.lpn_profile_edit_click: Drag any point on the path to move it. Select a point you added to take it off.
keys.lpn_profile_edit_tap: Drag any point on the path to move it. Select a point you added to take it off.
keys.lpn_profile_edit_nowhere: A point on the path has to be a node. The path is unchanged.
keys.lpn_profile_file_done: Profile read from the file: {used} of {total} nodes found in this network.
keys.lpn_profile_file_missing: Named in the file but not in this network: {ids}.
keys.lpn_profile_file_short: The file names fewer than two nodes in this network, so there is no profile to draw.
keys.lpn_profile_delete_confirm: Delete the saved path {name}? The drawing itself is not changed.
keys.lpn_profile_missing: The saved path {name} uses nodes that are not in this project: {ids}
keys.lpn_ts_tip: Graph one or more assets across an extended period simulation.
keys.lpn_pgraph_none: This asset has no results in the current run.
keys.lpn_result_pump_head_tip: The head the pump adds from suction to discharge, shown as a positive number. The solver and EPANET files carry it as a negative head loss.
keys.lpn_ts_none: Nothing to graph yet. Select assets on the map and press Add selected.
keys.lpn_ts_no_frames: No extended period results yet. Press Calculate to run the simulation.
keys.lpn_freq_none: No results for this value yet, so there is nothing to graph.
keys.lpn_contour_tip: Show a contour plot on the map: the node colors spread along and beside the pipes, with labeled contour lines. Opens a box to tune it or turn it off.
keys.lpn_contour_show_tip: Clear to hide the fill and the contour lines; check to bring them back as they were. Node colors stay.
keys.lpn_contour_fill_tip: Smooth blends the colors from one class to the next. Bands paints each class of the color key flat.
keys.lpn_contour_buffer_tip: Reach of the color from each pipe, as a multiple of the median pipe length. It fades out over the outer part.
keys.lpn_contour_support: Contour plot: {n} nodes, interpolated along {p} pipes and up to {k} times the median pipe length beside them. No color across pumps, valves, or closed links.
keys.lpn_contour_too_many: Too many contour lines at this interval; widen it to draw them.
keys.lpn_contour_dem: Ground between nodes from Mapbox DEM
keys.lpn_contour_dem_tip: Between nodes, pressure becomes the interpolated head minus the height of the ground from Mapbox DEM, so it can fall below the lowest node pressure on a hill the network has no node on. Treat the ground as a contour map, not a survey.
keys.lpn_contour_support_dem: Between nodes, pressure is the interpolated head minus the ground elevation from Mapbox DEM, sampled about every {m} m.
keys.lpn_contour_dem_failed: The ground could not be read from Mapbox DEM, so pressure is interpolated between nodes alone.
keys.lpn_contour_consent_1: Drawing pressure over the ground sends the area your network covers, as Mapbox map tile numbers, to api.mapbox.com, to read the height of the ground there.
keys.lpn_contour_consent_2: This is a different question from the map pictures behind your project. The pictures only say where you are looking. These tiles say where your network is. Mapbox will receive those tile numbers and your IP address. We send nothing else: no name, no pipes, no project. We keep no record of it, and nothing is stored on this device except your answer to this question.
keys.lpn_contour_consent_3: May we send the tile numbers of your network's area to Mapbox?
keys.lpn_contour_consent_4: If you say no, everything else on this page keeps working exactly as it does now, and the contour plot is drawn between nodes alone. We remember a yes so that we need not ask again. A no is not stored at all.
keys.lpn_sysflow_tip: Graph the total flow produced and the total flow consumed against time, across the extended period simulation. Tanks are in neither total, so where the two lines part, the tanks are filling or draining.
keys.lpn_sysflow_produced_tip: Total flow into the network from reservoirs and from negative demands.
keys.lpn_sysflow_consumed_tip: Total of every positive demand: water drawn from the network at junctions, and any flow into a reservoir.
keys.lpn_new_coordsys_tip: Choose the coordinate system of your network. The only way to change this choice is with “File, Convert as…” to a new project, and that conversion is approximate.
keys.lpn_new_coordsys_local_tip: Not georeferenced. Use the Map, World map… or Map, Background image… menu later if you wish to add a backdrop.
keys.lpn_crs_view_tip: Offer only the coordinate systems that cover the place the map is looking at. Clear it to read the whole list.
keys.lpn_crs_place_tip: Searches are sent to the OpenStreetMap place-name service, and permission is requested the first time. A new geographic project also starts at the place found here.
keys.lpn_crs_name_tip: Text that filters the list: only the coordinate systems whose name or EPSG code contains it are shown.
keys.lpn_crs_list_tip: The coordinate systems that pass the filters above. Choose one, then press OK.
keys.lpn_crs_noview: No place has been searched for yet, so the whole list is offered. Search for a place above or zoom the map to narrow it.
keys.lpn_crs_count_network: {n} of {total} coordinate systems cover this network.
keys.lpn_crs_unplaceable: {crs} is one of the few listed coordinate systems without usable projection information. This means that world map, place name search, and DEM elevations don't work. Your coordinates are unaffected.
keys.lpn_new_units_tip: Units and other settings are stored with each project, so this choice applies to this project only and is not saved as a browser setting. To reuse preferences, save an empty project as a template and start each new project from it.
keys.lpn_recent_denied: Permission to open that file was not given, so it was not opened.
keys.lpn_recent_gone: Could not open {file}. It may have been moved, renamed, or deleted, so it was taken off the recent list.
keys.lpn_import_bad_file: That file could not be read as a project saved from this page.
keys.lpn_import_no_room: There is not enough browser storage left to add this project. Delete a project you no longer need and try again.
keys.lpn_file_import_inp_tip: Create a new project from an EPANET file, or, when a project is open, update it from the file. The file is either the .inp export format (preferred) or the native .net format (last resort). To open an EPANET-MSX model as well, choose its .msx file at the same time.
keys.lpn_file_export_tables_tip: Download the tables as the Tables pane shows them, in one workbook with a sheet for each table (and for each scenario you choose), plus a sheet for each library their IDs refer to: patterns, curves, pipe types, and fittings. Results are included for the scenario last calculated only.
keys.lpn_file_export_csv_tip: Download a table as the Tables pane shows it. One table comes as a single CSV file with no libraries. Several tables or scenarios come as one zip file of CSV files, with a file for each library their IDs refer to. Results are included for the scenario last calculated only.
keys.lpn_file_export_inp_tip: Download this network as an EPANET .inp file (in a zip file with its image if applicable). Anything the .inp format cannot hold is listed for you afterwards.
keys.lpn_status_inp_exported_picture: Exported {zip}, holding the EPANET file {file}, its background picture {picture}, and the world file {world}. Extract all three into one folder, then open the .inp there in EPANET; the picture comes with it.
keys.lpn_status_inp_exported_no_picture: Exported {file}. The background picture could not be saved, so the .inp names none; in EPANET, add it with View > Backdrop > Load.
keys.lpn_inp_export_flat_customers_inactive: {n} of these customers are assigned to a junction that is inactive in this scenario, so their demand is not in the file.
keys.lpn_inp_export_flat_inactive_controls: These controls and rules refer to an asset that is inactive in this scenario, so they are not in the file: {ids}
keys.lpn_inp_export_difference_one: One thing the .inp format cannot hold.
keys.lpn_inp_export_refused: This project cannot be written as an EPANET file: {detail}
keys.lpn_file_export_dxf_tip: Download this network for AutoCAD and other CAD programs: nodes as symbol blocks, pipes, pumps, and valves as polylines, and every asset as a block whose attributes carry its ID and property values in the project units.
keys.lpn_dxf_export_no_utm: The DXF file was not written: this network lies outside the latitudes UTM covers (80° S to 84° N), and a drawing needs a flat grid to be drawn on.
keys.lpn_dxf_export_refused: The DXF file was not written: the coordinate conversion it needs did not load. Check the connection and try again.
keys.lpn_dxf_export_failed: The DXF file was not written: an error in this page stopped it ({error}).
keys.lpn_dxf_note_grid: Coordinates: the X and Y of this project, in {unit}. No coordinate system is stated.
keys.lpn_dxf_note_crs: Coordinates: {crs}, exactly as this project states them.
keys.lpn_dxf_note_geo: Coordinates: {crs}, in meters, not latitude and longitude. The latitudes and longitudes of the project were converted to that grid.
keys.lpn_dxf_exported_geo: Exported {file}. Its coordinates are {crs}, in meters, not latitude and longitude.
keys.lpn_dxf_note_blocks: Layers are named {prefix}, the asset code, a hyphen, and the alternative, as in {example}. Each element is a block inserted at scale 1 with attributes 1 unit high; scale the blocks to set the text height. Every attribute is visible; the attributes of one element are stacked in a column beside its symbol.
keys.lpn_dxf_note_shortened: Values longer than a DXF file allows ({max} characters): {n}. Each was shortened and ends in three periods.
keys.lpn_dxf_note_categories: Junctions with more than one demand category: {n}. Their {tag} attribute holds the sum of the base demands of all categories.
keys.lpn_file_export_geojson_tip: Download this network as a GeoJSON file for QGIS, ArcGIS Pro and other GIS programs. Junctions, tanks and reservoirs are points, and pipes, pumps and valves are lines that follow their vertices. Positions are latitude and longitude. Results are included only when the network has been solved.
keys.lpn_file_export_workspace_tip: Download a small file holding the layout of this page: where the panes, table columns and boxes sit, their sizes, and which are open, docked or hidden, plus the display options of this page, such as which help bubbles and the hover card are shown. Your projects, project settings and cookies (language, consent, units) are not in it. Load it on another screen or browser with File, Import, Workspace.
keys.lpn_file_import_workspace_tip: Apply a workspace file saved with File, Export, Workspace: the layout of the panes, table columns and boxes, and the display options of this page, such as which help bubbles and the hover card are shown. Your projects and cookies are not touched.
keys.lpn_file_import_msx_tip: Attach an EPANET-MSX file (.msx) to this project, or show the one already attached. It is kept with the project, written back unchanged, and run by the EPANET-MSX engine in an extended period simulation.
keys.lpn_file_export_msx_tip: Download the attached EPANET-MSX file exactly as it was imported.
keys.lpn_msx_report_kept: This EPANET-MSX file is kept with the project and written back unchanged when the EPANET-MSX file is exported. Water quality is set to Multi-species (EPANET-MSX) under Settings, Calculation, Quality, so an extended period simulation runs every species in the file.
keys.lpn_msx_report_no_species: No species are listed in the file.
keys.lpn_msx_too_big: {file} is too large to keep in browser storage, so it was not attached.
keys.lpn_msx_report_missing: IDs in the file that this network does not have: {ids}.
keys.lpn_msx_not_msx: {file} does not look like an EPANET-MSX file: it has no [SPECIES] section.
keys.lpn_quality_msx_species_tip: The EPANET-MSX species the map colors, the Tables pane and the Graph pane show. Every species in the file is computed in the same run, so changing this needs no new run. Values are in the units the EPANET-MSX file declares: mass per liter for a bulk species, mass per unit area for a wall species.
keys.lpn_quality_msx_none: No EPANET-MSX file is attached to this project. Attach one with File, Import, EPANET-MSX file.
keys.lpn_result_msx_tip: The value of this EPANET-MSX species, computed by the EPANET-MSX engine, in the units the EPANET-MSX file declares. For a link it is the average along the link.
keys.lpn_workspace_imported: Workspace applied from {file}. Settings applied: {n}. Returned to their defaults: {r}.
keys.lpn_workspace_ignored: Entries ignored because they were not recognized: {u}.
keys.lpn_workspace_refused_unreadable: This file could not be read as a workspace, so nothing was changed.
keys.lpn_workspace_refused_format: This is not a workspace file saved by this page, so nothing was changed.
keys.lpn_workspace_refused_newer: This workspace file was saved by a newer version of this page (format {version}), so nothing was changed.
keys.lpn_workspace_confirm: Replace this browser's workspace layout with the one in the file?
keys.lpn_workspace_refused_storage: Browser storage is full or unavailable, so the workspace was not applied.
keys.lpn_geojson_refused_local: A GeoJSON file holds latitude and longitude only, and this project is drawn on a local grid with no place on the Earth. Georeference it first with Map, World map, Attach, then export again.
keys.lpn_geojson_refused_range: These positions are not valid latitudes and longitudes: {detail}
keys.lpn_geojson_refused_crs: The coordinate system of this project ({detail}) is not known to this page, so its positions cannot be converted to latitude and longitude. Use Convert as… to copy the project into one this page knows, then export again.
keys.lpn_geojson_refused_empty: There is nothing to export yet. Draw or open a network first.
keys.lpn_geojson_results_in: The results on screen are included.
keys.lpn_geojson_results_out: No results are included, because the network is not solved.
keys.lpn_inp_bad_file: That file could not be read as an EPANET network file.
keys.lpn_net_bad_file: This looks like an EPANET .net file, but this page could not read it. Open it in EPANET and use the File, Export, Network command there to save it as an .inp file, then import that.
keys.lpn_inp_report_counts: {nodes} junctions, reservoirs and tanks, {links} pipes, pumps and valves, in {units}.
keys.lpn_inp_report_clean: All data in the file was imported. Nothing was omitted.
keys.lpn_inp_report_label_anchor: Text labels are placed as EPANET places them, from their top left corner.
keys.lpn_inp_report_no_crs: EPANET files contain no coordinate system, so this file will not initially be georeferenced. To place it on a world map, use Map, World map… To convert its coordinates, use File, Convert as…
keys.lpn_inp_backdrop_attach_tip: A web page cannot open the picture by its name. Choose it on your device and it is placed where the file says it belongs.
keys.lpn_inp_backdrop_attached: Attached {file}, placed where the file says it belongs.
keys.lpn_inp_backdrop_attached_other: Attached {picked}, placed where the file says it belongs. The file names {file}, which is a different name.
keys.lpn_inp_report_lead: This page does not use every EPANET feature, but no data in the file is discarded. The list below shows data in the file that is retained but not used, and any changes made during import:
keys.lpn_inp_drop_headloss: This file does not use the Hazen-Williams formula. This page computes Hazen-Williams, so the pipe roughness numbers were kept exactly as written, but the results here will not match the results in EPANET.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_tank_curve: These tanks are not straight-sided: the file gives their shape as a volume curve. The curve is kept in the Libraries box, the tank still refers to it, and an extended period simulation uses it to compute the level as the tank fills and drains. A single-period analysis is unaffected, because the water surface is at the level stated in the file. The diameter in the file is kept beside the curve and is used to draw and solve a tank with no curve.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_tcv: These throttle valves were imported as throttle valves, with the loss stated in the file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_valve_active: These valves control pressure or flow, and their status changes with hydraulic conditions. They were imported without loss of data, and this page solves them.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_valve: These valves are described by a curve or by a fixed pressure drop, and this page has no such asset. They were imported as open pipes, so the network remains connected, but pressure and flow are no longer controlled at those locations.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_cv: In EPANET these pipes allow flow in one direction only (check valves). They were imported as ordinary pipes, so flow may now pass in either direction.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_demands: These junctions had more than one demand. The demands were added together into the single demand this page holds.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_patterns: This page did not read the demand patterns, because the extended period simulation module did not load. Every demand is the value stated in the file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_demand_pattern: These junctions have demands that vary over the run. Their patterns were imported in full, and the demand shown is the value at the time on the clock.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_emitters: These junctions have a sprinkler or leak coefficient. It was kept, it is being solved, and each of them shows it in the Emitter coefficient box in its properties.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_curve_long: This pump curve had more than three points. Its lowest, middle and highest points were kept, because this page fits a curve to three points at most.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_curve_missing: This pump refers to a curve that is not in the file. The pump was imported without a curve, so it adds no head.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_pump_other: This pump is described by the power it draws, rather than by a curve. It was imported without a curve, so it adds no head.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_head_pattern: These reservoirs have a head that varies over the run. Their patterns were imported in full, and the water level shown is the value at the time on the clock.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_pump_speed: These pumps run at a speed other than the speed at which their curve was measured, or change speed over the run. The speed and its pattern were imported in full, and the head shown is the value at the time on the clock.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_setting: These pipes, pumps, and valves have a setting this page cannot hold. They were imported as open.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_rules: This file has rule-based controls. This page reads and applies them. When the model is run, the rules are applied, with every level, pressure, and flow in them converted to the units this project displays. Open Rules under Libraries to view or edit a rule. Rules are kept exactly as stated in the file and are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_eps: This file describes an extended period simulation. The extended period simulation module of this page did not load, so only the initial conditions were imported.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_quality: This file describes water quality: initial concentrations and reaction rates in pipes and tanks. This page reads and uses those values. Choose a chemical under Settings, Calculation, Quality, then run the model to compute concentrations throughout the network over the run. The lines are kept and are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_sources_mixing: This file states where a chemical is injected into the network and how water mixes in each tank. Each source is shown on the node where it is applied, and each tank shows its mixing model. Both are used when the network is run over a total run time.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_energy: This EPANET file includes pumping cost modelling data. This page reads it and uses it. Run the model, then open Water, Reports, Pump energy to see how long each pump ran, the power it drew, the energy it used and what that cost. The lines are kept, and they are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_tags: This file assigns tags to some junctions, pipes, or other assets. Every tag was imported and appears in the properties of its asset, where it can be viewed or edited.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_report: This file contains EPANET report-format settings. The run report is available under Reports, Run, but it uses the standard EPANET format rather than the format these settings specify. The lines are kept and are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_sections: This file holds a section that this page does not read at all. Nothing here uses it. It is kept whole, and it is written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_comments: These comment lines in the patterns or simple controls of this file were not imported, because this page has no place to keep them (for example, between the rows of one pattern). Every pattern and control was imported in full.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_quality_options: This file states EPANET water quality options: the Quality option, which names the kind of water quality analysis, and two settings that go with a chemical, Relative diffusivity and Quality tolerance. All three are kept and used. Water age, source trace, and a chemical are each computed here, and the two chemical settings are used when a chemical is run. All of them are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_file_options: This file refers to an auxiliary file: Map, which holds coordinates, or Hydraulics, which holds previously computed hydraulics. This page cannot open either, so the lines are kept as they are and written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_other_options: This file states options this page does not read. Nothing here uses them. They are kept and are written back if you save an EPANET file.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_net_options: This EPANET .net file states settings that this page has no control for, so their values are listed here rather than carried across. Everything else came over. If you need them, open the file in EPANET and use File, Export, Network to save it as an .inp file, then import that.
keys.lpn_net_emergency: This was an EPANET .net file, the native EPANET project format. The format has no published specification; this page reads it using a format inferred from example files, so use it only when no .inp file is available. The .inp file is the documented format that other programs read: in EPANET use File, Export, Network to write one, and import that file instead whenever possible.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_backdrop: This file names a background picture but does not contain the picture itself. Add it yourself with File, Background image, Add image.

keys.lpn_notes_1_def: By default the network is solved by the EPANET solver. When a total run time is set, each reporting time step is calculated in sequence: tanks fill and drain, demands follow their patterns, and the toolbar plays back the run. With Use the built-in solver when possible checked, a single instant solution can be solved by the built-in solver instead, but an extended period simulation is always solved by the EPANET solver.
keys.lpn_notes_2_def: Surge and water hammer are not modeled: all results are for steady or slowly varying flow, not for the transient pressure wave caused by rapid valve closure. Multi-species water quality (EPANET-MSX) is not modeled. Water age, source trace, and one reacting chemical are.
keys.lpn_notes_3_def: Every project is a tab, and every tab is saved in this browser as the work proceeds. Clearing the browser's data deletes them all, so the work belongs in a file: File, Save as. An asterisk on a tab means it holds changes that are not in a file, and closing that tab asks first. Nothing is ever written to a file unless Save or Save as is chosen. In some browsers a project connects to the file it is saved to, and File, Save writes back to that same file from then on; in others no connection is possible, so Save is disabled and only Save as is available. This site keeps track of who has a project file open, so that two people do not write over each other. Opening a file that a colleague already has open offers Ask, Open read-only, and Break lock. If the server cannot be reached, a warning states that another user can edit the same file at the same time.
keys.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. The points of the curve are entered in Water, Libraries, as a Pump head curve, and the pump states that curve in Properties. Three points, the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow, fit H₀, a, and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses EPANET’s rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33334 times the head entered, and the highest flow is 2 times the flow entered, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no curve stated adds no head. The curve is not truncated where the head reaches zero, so a flow greater than the curve can deliver produces a negative head. The remedy is a larger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit. A curve can hold more than three points. The EPANET solver is given all of them and interpolates between them, while the Equation line and the built-in solver use the lowest, middle, and highest points.

keys.lpn_notes_color_def: Color band boundaries are set when a data classification method is chosen. They are not set again at each time step, because that would make the colors mean something new at every step, which is not helpful for visualizing a system. A scenario shows the boundaries of Base. EPANET works the same way. To get new boundaries, choose a method again or enter boundaries.
keys.lpn_notes_engine_def: The EPANET solver on this page is OWA-EPANET 2.3.5, released on 20 February 2025. EPANET is developed by Open Water Analytics, a community that works with the United States Environmental Protection Agency, which released version 2.2.0 in December 2019. The run report calls it 2.3.05 because the engine writes the last number in two digits. It is delivered to this page through epanet-js 0.9.0 by Luke Butler, under the MIT license, and it runs in the browser: the network is never sent to a server to be solved.
keys.lpn_guide_nt_example_term: Example on Net1: a pump past its curve
keys.lpn_guide_nt_example_def: Open the Net1 example and choose Water, Libraries. Curve 1, Pump Curve for Pump 9, has one point, 1500 gpm at 250 ft. The head at zero flow is 333.3 ft and the highest flow is 3000 gpm. At 3500 gpm, which is past the end of the curve, the curve gives a head of −120.4 ft. The EPANET solver reports that same head, a loss of 120.4 ft across the pump, and warns that pumps cannot deliver enough flow or head.
keys.lpn_guide_own_example_def: Open the Net1 example, press Ctrl+K, and type critical. Menus shows the row Criticality analysis… under Water, Analyze. Boxes shows the entries that mention it, among them Find and replace, Fire flow analysis, and Criticality analysis, and this entry. Choosing the row shows where Criticality analysis… is in the Analyze menu, and does not run it.

keys.lpn_field_valve_type_tip: Valve type. A throttle valve (TCV) applies a fixed loss. PRV, PSV, and FCV maintain a pressure or a flow, and open fully, close, or partly close as hydraulic conditions change. A PBV removes a fixed pressure, and a GPV follows a head loss curve. The types control different hydraulic properties, so settings may be lost when the type is changed.
keys.lpn_field_valve_setting_drop_tip: The pressure lost at the valve. A pressure breaker valve always removes exactly this much pressure, whichever way the water is going. It is a drop across the valve, not a pressure to hold.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_gpv_curve: This valve refers to a head loss curve that is not in the file. The valve was imported without a curve, so it remains fully open until a curve is chosen.
keys.lpn_gpv_curve_source_tip: The curve in the Libraries box that gives the head loss through this valve at each flow. Several valves can use the same curve, and editing it there changes all of them.
keys.lpn_field_valve_setting_pressure_tip: A pressure reducing valve keeps the pressure on its downstream side at or below this value. A pressure sustaining valve keeps the pressure on its upstream side at or above this value.
keys.lpn_field_valve_setting_flow_tip: Maximum flow through the valve. When the flow is less than this value, the valve is fully open and adds no loss.
keys.lpn_field_valve_setting_loss_tip: Head removed by the throttle valve, as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 for a fully open valve. This one value is the entire loss of a throttle valve.
keys.lpn_field_valve_diameter_tip: Diameter of the valve opening. The velocity through the valve is computed from this diameter, and the loss from that velocity.
keys.lpn_field_valve_km_tip: Loss through the valve body when the valve is fully open, in addition to any loss from the valve setting. It is expressed as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 to ignore it.
keys.lpn_pump_curve_source_tip: The curve in the Libraries box that gives the head this pump adds at each flow. Several pumps can use the same curve, and editing it there changes all of them.
keys.lpn_field_tag_tip: A one-word identifier with any meaning you require, such as a pressure zone or a work order.
keys.lpn_pump_effic_curve_tip: The curve in the Libraries box that gives the efficiency of this pump at each flow. Several pumps can use the same curve, and editing it there changes all of them. This pump holds only the reference; the points themselves are read and edited under Libraries, Curves.
keys.lpn_curve_library_link_tip: Open the Libraries box on its Curves section, where a curve is added, described, edited and deleted. An asset states which curve it uses.

keys.lpn_sm_help:
How scenarios and alternatives work:

In Basic mode, alternatives are hidden and automatic, and all new scenarios are children of the Base scenario.

With Basic mode off, a complex inheritance tree is available, and alternatives can be shared among scenarios. But the default behavior of edits when a new alternative association is needed (in the absence of proactive user management) is to create an alternative named like the current scenario, which gives each scenario its unique set of alternatives.

Properties and settings belong to alternatives categories that appear as columns of the scenarios and alternatives table and as management options in Scenario manager.

Overrides are created in scenarios, but they really belong to the respective alternatives associated with the scenario; so a scenario is like a window to its alternatives. Associations of alternatives to scenarios are managed in the second pane of the Scenario manager or in the Scenarios table in the bottom pane. Creating a new scenario creates no alternatives; the new scenario uses its parent's alternatives until overrides are created that need new alternatives. When overrides are created in a scenario, they are stored in their respective alternative for the scenario; if the scenario has no such alternative, a new alternative is created using the name of the scenario.

Example: You create a "Figure: Node and link IDs" scenario and edit a Text to say "Node and Link IDs." When you create the scenario, no alternatives are created. But at the moment you save the Text, a Text alternative called "Figure: Node and link IDs" is created with the override for the Text value. In Basic mode, you see this as simply an override in the scenario itself.

Copy properties copies only overrides. In any scenario other than Base, it copies only the overrides the asset has in that scenario.

How to manage scenarios:

- Choose Scenarios or an alternatives category in the list at the top to show its tree.

- Create a child of the selected item with Add child. Add base adds another Base, which starts as a copy of Base as it is now; later edits to Base do not change it. A new child is named after its parent; type a name to rename it. Copy copies the selected alternative. Merge upward moves the overrides of the selected alternative into an alternative above it, chosen by name, and the selected alternative then inherits them; it first names any value an alternative it skips also overrides, which is not changed. To copy a scenario, use Copy scenario in the Scenarios menu, in Basic mode; it copies the scenario's overrides, with the alternatives that hold them. Add base and Copy scenario each create alternatives: Add base creates a Base alternative for the new Base in each category that holds values, and Copy scenario creates a new alternative, named like the copy, for each alternative that holds the scenario's overrides.

- Drag an item onto another to make it a child of that item. A scenario moved to a new parent inherits from it everything it has not overridden; what it has overridden does not change. Drag an item between two items to reorder them.

- Click an item to select it. Press F2 or choose Rename to rename the selected item. Renaming a scenario asks whether to rename the alternatives that carry its name; in Basic mode they are renamed with it, without asking. Double-click a scenario or press Enter to make it current. Click the arrow beside an item or press Left or Right to collapse or expand it. Right-click an item for the same commands as the buttons.

- Press Delete or click the minus button to delete the selected item. An item in use is not deleted, and the message names what uses it. Deleting a scenario with Basic mode off keeps the alternatives it uses. Deleting a scenario with Basic mode on also deletes each of its alternatives that no other scenario uses.

- To make a scenario use another alternative, including Base, choose it in the scenario's row of the second pane of the Scenario manager or the Scenarios table. An override made in a shared alternative changes every scenario that uses it.
