keys.lpn_time_no_engine: The built-in solver solves one instant at a time, so this is the network at {time} only: every pattern is read at that instant, and every tank remains at its initial level instead of filling and draining. Connect to the internet once to download the EPANET solver, which runs an extended period simulation.
keys.lpn_time_no_engine_why: The built-in solver solves one instant at a time, so this is the network at {time} only: every pattern is read at that instant, and every tank remains at its initial level instead of filling and draining. {reason}
keys.lpn_time_engine_fetch_failed: The download of the EPANET solver failed. Reload the page to try again; a firewall, proxy, or browser extension may be blocking it.
keys.lpn_time_engine_start_failed: The browser refused to start the EPANET solver. WebAssembly may be turned off by a security setting or an extension.
keys.lpn_time_engine_run_failed: The EPANET run failed. That is a defect in this page; use the {wrong} link to report it.
keys.lpn_time_no_period: This project has no extended period simulation set, so there is only one moment to show. Set a Total run time in Settings, Calculation, Time to run an extended period simulation.
keys.lpn_time_run_done: The run finished. Reporting time steps: {frames}. Time taken: {secs} s.
keys.lpn_time_runbox_hide: Do not show this box again
keys.lpn_settings_runbox_tip: A box that reports the progress and outcome of a run. With it turned off, a finished run says the same thing in the status line for a few seconds instead. This is a setting for this browser, not for the project.
keys.lpn_time_run_failed: The run did not finish, so there are no results for the later times.
keys.lpn_time_run_report_tip: The report EPANET wrote for the last run, verbatim: whether it converged, and any warnings. The text is produced by the EPANET solver, not by this page.
keys.lpn_settings_search_tip: Enter a word or multiple words to see settings that mention all of them.
keys.lpn_setbox_divider: Width of the Settings section list
keys.lpn_rpane_empty: Nothing is docked here yet. Everything that belongs to the whole project is in Settings.
keys.lpn_labels_customer_note: A customer label shows the values chosen here. It is drawn at the same text size as every other label on the map.
keys.lpn_labels_customer_width_tip: Customer labels are drawn only while the map view is this wide or narrower. Leave the box blank to draw them at every zoom. Enter 0 to never draw a customer label, at any zoom. This has no effect if it is larger than the similar setting for all labels.
keys.lpn_settings_quality_track_tip: Choose what the run should trace through the network: how long the water has been in the system, where it came from, or a chemical that reacts as it travels. Only a chemical needs coefficients.
keys.lpn_settings_quality_source_tip: The node whose water is traced. Every other node then shows the share of its water that came from that node.
keys.lpn_quality_needs_run: Water quality is carried along the pipes as the water travels, so it needs an extended period simulation. Set a Total run time under Time, then press the Calculate button.
keys.lpn_quality_chemical_name_tip: The chemical being tracked, for example Chlorine. Leave it blank to use the EPANET default label, Chemical. Shown on reports, but not used in the calculations.
keys.lpn_quality_mass_units_tip: The units part of the quality entry, from the two EPANET choices.
keys.lpn_quality_tolerance_tip: Concentration difference below which EPANET treats two adjoining parcels of water as one. Blank uses the EPANET default of 0.01.
keys.lpn_quality_diffusivity_tip: Diffusivity of the chemical in water, relative to chlorine. Blank uses the EPANET default of 1.0.
keys.lpn_quality_initial_tip: Amount of the chemical at this node when the run starts. A reservoir keeps this value for the whole run, which is how the residual leaving a treatment plant is usually stated. Blank means 0.
keys.lpn_result_concentration_tip: Amount of the chemical remaining at this point after transport and reaction. The units are those entered with the chemical name under Settings, Calculation, Quality.
keys.lpn_source_type_tip: What kind of chemical source dosing is applied here based on the Source Quality value? Concentration source uses the value as a concentration applied to the external inflow (reservoir or negative demand). Mass booster adds a fixed mass flow per minute to that entering the node from other points in the network. Setpoint booster ensures that the concentration leaving the node is no lower than the value. Flow-paced booster source adds a fixed concentration to that resulting from the mixing of all inflow to the node from other points in the network
keys.lpn_source_quality_tip: Strength of the dose. For every type but the mass booster this is a concentration, in the units named beside the chemical under Settings, Calculation, Quality; for a mass booster it is a mass flow per minute. Blank means no chemical source, functionally equivalent to 0.
keys.lpn_source_pattern_tip: A time pattern that scales the dose through the run, for a feed that is not constant. No pattern means that the dose is the same at every step.
keys.lpn_mixing_model_tip: Model of how the water already in this tank mixes with the inflow. Complete mixing mixes all inflow instantly with the entire tank volume. Two-compartment mixing fills an inlet zone first and passes the overflow to the main zone. FIFO plug flow discharges water in the order it arrived. LIFO plug flow stacks it, so the last water in is the first water out. The choice affects water age and residual, not pressure or flow.
keys.lpn_mixing_fraction_tip: The share of the tank volume that the inlet zone takes up, between 0 and 1. Only two-compartment mixing uses it. Blank means that the whole tank is the inlet zone.
keys.lpn_reaction_bulk_tip: Reaction in the body of the water (see EPANET Help), used for every pipe and tank that has no individual coefficient. A negative number decays the chemical and a positive one increases it. Blank means no bulk reaction.
keys.lpn_reaction_wall_tip: Reaction at the pipe wall (see EPANET Help) used for every pipe with no entry. A negative number decays the chemical. Blank means no wall reaction.
keys.lpn_reaction_pipe_tip: Reaction in the body of the water (see EPANET Help). A negative number decays the chemical and a positive one increases it. Blank means to use the coefficient set for the whole network under Settings, Calculation, Quality.
keys.lpn_reaction_tank_tip: Reaction in the water held in this tank, as a rate in 1/day. A negative number decays the chemical and a positive one increases it. Water stands in a tank far longer than it stands in any pipe, so this is often where a residual is lost. Blank means to use the bulk reaction coefficient set for the whole network under Settings, Calculation, Quality.
keys.lpn_reaction_order_bulk_tip: The exponent the concentration is raised to for reaction in the body of the water. Any real number is allowed. 1 is the default value and is used for most chlorine decay modelling. 0 makes the rate independent of how much chemical is there.
keys.lpn_reaction_order_tank_tip: The exponent the concentration is raised to for reaction in the water held in a tank, separate from the bulk reaction order so a tank can react on a different order from the pipes. Any real number is allowed, and 1 is the default. EPANET states it as ORDER TANK in a file and has no input for it in the EPANET interface.
keys.lpn_reaction_order_wall_tip: 1 means that the wall reaction is dependent on the concentration in the bulk flow. 0 means it is not.
keys.lpn_reaction_limiting_tip: A concentration the chemical moves toward instead of decaying to nothing or growing without end. The reaction slows as the water approaches it and stops there. Use consistent units. No limit if blank.
keys.lpn_reaction_rough_corr_tip: Factor that correlates the wall reaction coefficient with the roughness of each pipe, so a rougher pipe reacts faster. When it is set, a wall coefficient is computed for each pipe from its roughness, and the single wall coefficient above is not used. Not used if blank.
keys.lpn_reaction_note: This application offers no reaction coefficient suggestions. There is no standard test for one, and published field values for the same kind of water differ by a factor of ten. Enter one you have measured or one you can cite, or leave the boxes empty for a chemical that does not react.
keys.lpn_energy_efficiency_tip: The wire-to-water efficiency used for every pump that has no efficiency curve. EPANET uses 75 percent when no value is stated.
keys.lpn_energy_price_tip: Cost of one kilowatt hour. It applies to every pump that has no individual price. Blank means 0.
keys.lpn_energy_pump_price_tip: Cost of one kilowatt hour at this pump. Blank means to use the price set for the whole network under Settings, Energy.
keys.lpn_energy_price_pattern_tip: A pattern that multiplies the price at each pattern step, which is how an off-peak rate is specified. Leave it empty for constant price throughout the run.
keys.lpn_energy_demand_charge_tip: Per kW, for the peak load demanded by the pumps
keys.lpn_energy_currency_tip: Text printed beside every cost value. It is a label only; use one currency throughout.
keys.lpn_energy_price_note: This application offers no price suggestions. What power costs depends on the utility, the country, the hour and the year.
keys.lpn_energy_needs_run: Pump energy is power integrated over the run, so it needs an extended period simulation. Set a Total run time in Settings, Calculation, Time, press the Calculate button, then open Water, Reports, Pump energy.
keys.lpn_energy_no_pumps: This network has no pumps, so there is nothing drawing power.
keys.lpn_scncmp_menu_tip: Table of scenarios with count of overrides, lowest pressure, and highest velocity, and a table of results by asset that copies to a spreadsheet
keys.lpn_scncmp_empty: Nothing has been drawn yet, so there is nothing to solve.
keys.lpn_scncmp_period_note: Where a scenario has a total run time, its lowest pressure and highest velocity are the extremes of the whole network, at the time shown.
keys.lpn_scncmp_note: Every scenario is solved from a copy of the drawing. Nothing here changes the project, and the scenario you are working in is left as it was.
keys.lpn_scncmp_stopped: Stopped after {done} of {total} scenarios. The results below are the ones already finished.
keys.lpn_scnres_none: Check at least one result to show.
keys.lpn_scnres_empty: This project has none of these assets.
keys.lpn_scnres_copy_tip: Copy the table as tab-separated text, to paste into a spreadsheet. Numbers are copied in full, without rounding.
keys.lpn_scnres_time_note: A scenario with a total run time is read at the time step on screen, {time}, or at its last time step if its run ends sooner. Each heading shows the time read.
keys.lpn_scnres_not_converged_note: A column marked {mark} shows the last results the solver reached before it stopped without converging.
keys.lpn_scnres_failed: {scenario} could not be solved, so its columns are blank. {why}
keys.lpn_scnres_flow_tip: The sign of a flow is the solver's internal direction sign. It has no use outside the solver except to show here whether a flow changed direction between scenarios.
keys.lpn_scnres_stale: Recalculate is off, so the results on the map and in the Tables pane are from an earlier solve. The {scenario} columns here are solved from the current inputs and may differ from them.
keys.lpn_energy_col_avg_kw_tip: The average power used when this pump was running. It is not averaged over idle periods so that a pump that was idle for much of the extended period simulation still reports the power it used while it ran.
keys.lpn_reports_status_tip: Chronological table of status changes read from the EPANET time steps of the last extended period simulation: pumps and valves opening or closing, tanks filling, emptying, filling up or running dry, and steps that did not fully converge.
keys.lpn_status_needs_run: The status report lists what changed during an extended period simulation. Set a Total run time in Settings, Calculation, Time, press Calculate, then open Water, Reports, Status changes.
keys.lpn_status_empty: Nothing changed status during this run.
keys.lpn_status_no_converge: The hydraulic solution at this step did not fully converge; the numbers shown are its last iteration.
keys.lpn_status_note: Read from the same extended period run as the Tables pane and the Full report. Only a change is listed, not every step.
keys.lpn_reports_full_tip: Table of all nodes and links at every reporting time step of the last run
keys.lpn_full_needs_run: The full report lists every node and every link at every reporting time step. Press Calculate, then open Water, Reports, Full.
keys.lpn_full_note: One row per node or link per reporting time step, in the units shown on the Tables pane. A blank cell is a column that quantity does not have. Download or print carries every time step; the table below shows one at a time.
keys.lpn_reports_calib_tip: Compare measured field data from a calibration file with the last run: statistics, a correlation plot, and mean comparisons.
keys.lpn_calib_param_tip: The quantity the calibration file measures. One file is held for each parameter.
keys.lpn_calib_load_tip: A text file with a location ID, a time, and a measured value on each line. The time is measured from the start of the simulation, in decimal hours or hours:minutes. A semicolon starts a comment. A line with only a time and a value belongs to the location above it.
keys.lpn_calib_none: No calibration file is loaded for this parameter.
keys.lpn_calib_session: A calibration file is held for this session only. It is not saved with the project or on this device.
keys.lpn_calib_units: The file's values are read in this project's units: {unit}.
keys.lpn_calib_missing: Named in the file but not in this network: {ids}.
keys.lpn_calib_missing_count: Measurements skipped because their location is not in this network: {n}.
keys.lpn_calib_bad_lines: Lines that could not be read, skipped: {lines}
keys.lpn_calib_outside: Measurements outside the times this run reported, skipped: {n}.
keys.lpn_calib_no_value: Measurements with no computed value at their time, skipped: {n}.
keys.lpn_calib_single: This is a single-period run, so every measurement is compared with its one result, whatever time the file gives.
keys.lpn_calib_needs_run: There are no results to compare with yet. The report fills in once the network has been calculated.
keys.lpn_calib_no_pairs: No measurement could be compared, so there is nothing to plot.
keys.lpn_calib_col_mean_err_tip: The mean of the absolute differences between each observed value and the computed value at the same time.
keys.lpn_calib_col_rms_err_tip: Root mean square error: the square root of the mean of the squared differences between observed and computed values.
keys.lpn_calib_corr_none: Correlation between means: it needs at least two locations whose means differ.
keys.lpn_calib_corr_note: Each point is one measurement. The closer the points lie to the diagonal line, the closer the computed values match the observed ones.
keys.lpn_calib_ts_note: Rings are measured values from the calibration file.
keys.lpn_energy_no_price: No price of power is stated, so every cost here is zero. Set one under Settings, Energy.
keys.lpn_energy_price_zero: This network states a price of zero, so every cost here is zero. Change it under Settings, Energy.
keys.lpn_energy_curve_note: These pumps call an efficiency curve with no points: {ids}. They ran at the efficiency set for the whole network.
keys.lpn_library_patterns_tip: A pattern is a list of multipliers that repeats. Each one applies for one pattern time step, so 24 numbers on a one hour step make a day that repeats. A demand of 10 with a multiplier of 1.5 is 15 at that moment.
keys.lpn_library_curves_tip: Pump head or efficiency vs flow, Valve loss vs flow, or Tank volume vs depth
keys.lpn_library_curves_note: Curves are attached to pumps and valves. For a pump head curve the run uses a curve fitted through the points as shown; for every other kind it connects the points with straight lines as shown.
keys.lpn_library_curve_equation_tip: The curve fitted through the given points and used for the pump model.
keys.lpn_library_curve_values_tip: Select one or two columns in a spreadsheet, copy them, and paste into the first target cell. Rows are added as needed. Lines copied directly from an EPANET file, including the curve name, can also be pasted.
keys.lpn_library_curve_copy_tip: Copy every point as two columns, ready to paste into a spreadsheet.
keys.lpn_library_curve_in_use: This curve is used by elements ({count}): {ids}. Assign another curve to them first, then delete this one.
keys.lpn_library_pipetypes_tip: A pipe type is a definition several pipes can refer to for their diameter, roughness and reaction coefficients. Editing the definition edits every pipe that uses it.
keys.lpn_library_pipetypes_note: Each project has a separate pipe type library. Properties may be left blank in a pipe type definition; for example, a pipe type may specify a roughness and no diameter. Pipe types are assigned to pipes in the pipe properties. Editing a definition here changes every pipe that references it.
keys.lpn_library_pipetype_blank_tip: Blank properties in a pipe type definition are left to be entered individually for each pipe.
keys.lpn_library_pipetype_in_use: This pipe type is used by pipes ({count}): {ids}. Detach it from them before deleting it.
keys.lpn_field_pipetype_tip: The pipe type in the project library that this pipe uses. Properties included in the pipe type are disabled for editing here. Detach the pipe type to enable editing here.
keys.lpn_pipetype_detach_tip: Copy the values this pipe reads from its type into the pipe itself and stop using the type. The pipe’s values don’t change now, and from now on these values are edited here.
keys.lpn_library_fittings_tip: Fittings with minor loss coefficients grouped into lists
keys.lpn_library_fittings_note: Each project has a separate fittings library. A fittings list has fittings with a quantity for each one, and it adds up to a single minor loss coefficient. Both pipes and pipe types may refer to a list.
keys.lpn_library_fittings_source: The fittings offered here are the thirteen in Table 3.3 of the EPANET 2.2 user manual. Choosing one copies its coefficient into the row, where it can be changed. A coefficient depends on the size and the make of the fitting, so treat the table as a starting point, not as final values.
keys.lpn_library_fittings_in_use: This fittings list is used by pipes ({count}): {ids}. Detach it from them before deleting it.
keys.lpn_library_import_tip: Choose another project file and copy whole libraries from it into this project. Anything whose name is already taken here is skipped and listed, so nothing you already have is changed.
keys.lpn_library_import_note: Each library you check is copied in whole. Delete what you do not want afterwards, the way you delete any other entry.
keys.lpn_library_import_no_libraries: That project file has no libraries to copy.
keys.lpn_library_import_conflict: Skipped, because this project already has one of the same name: {names}. Nothing here was changed. Rename either one and import again if you want both.
keys.lpn_library_import_none: That project file has none of these to copy.
keys.lpn_library_import_curve_shape: These curves were imported exactly as written in the file, and a run cannot use one until its first column rises from each point to the next: {names}
keys.lpn_library_import_needs_fittings: These pipe types refer to a fittings list this project does not have: {names}. Import the fittings library from the same file to resolve these references.
keys.lpn_library_import_units: Warning: Units mismatch. Will be imported as is. Not recommended.
keys.lpn_library_import_units_line: {name}: this project shows {mine}, the file shows {theirs}.
keys.lpn_field_fittings_tip: A list of fittings from the project library. The quantities and coefficients in the list are summed into this pipe's minor loss coefficient, and the coefficient box is read only. To enter the coefficient directly, leave the list unchosen.
keys.lpn_inp_export_flat_lead: The exported EPANET file is numerically equivalent to this project. But it has no place for the following things:
keys.lpn_inp_export_flat_types: Pipes ({n}) here refer to pipe types ({t}). In the file each of those pipes carries its own copy of the numbers, so the answers are the same. What the file cannot hold is the pipe type itself, so the link between one definition and every pipe that uses it is recorded only in the project file.
keys.lpn_inp_export_flat_coords: An EPANET file holds one position for each node. This scenario places {n} of them somewhere else, and those are the positions in the file. Every other scenario keeps its positions in the project file only.
keys.lpn_inp_export_flat_fittings: An EPANET file cannot hold the list of elbows, valves and tees in your project file. The minor loss coefficient of pipes here ({n}) is added up from a fittings list. The total goes into the file exactly as it stands, so nothing about the answers changes.
keys.lpn_library_controls_tip: A control is one statement that opens or closes a link, or changes its setting, based on a tank water level, a node pressure, or the time.
keys.lpn_library_pattern_values_tip: The multipliers, separated by spaces or commas. Paste a column from a spreadsheet if you have one. The list repeats for as long as the run lasts, so it does not have to cover the whole run.
keys.lpn_settings_default_pattern_tip: Every junction with no pattern uses this one.
keys.lpn_junction_pattern_unknown: No pattern in this project has the ID {id}, so the junction was left as it was.
keys.lpn_library_pattern_default_tip: The default demand pattern. Change it in Settings, Default demand pattern.
keys.lpn_library_pattern_default_deleted_to: Pattern {id} was the default demand pattern. Junctions with no pattern now use pattern {now}.
keys.lpn_library_pattern_default_deleted_none: Pattern {id} was the default demand pattern. Junctions with no pattern now use a constant demand.
keys.lpn_library_pattern_default_deleted_also: Scenarios that also used it as their default: {list}.
keys.lpn_library_pattern_default_deleted_in: Pattern {id} was the default demand pattern in these scenarios: {list}.
keys.lpn_library_control_tip: A one-line rule using EPANET syntax. Use consistent project units. Keywords must be in English. Examples: LINK 12 CLOSED IF NODE 23 ABOVE 20 (Link 12 will be closed when the level in Tank 23 exceeds 20 ft); LINK 12 OPEN IF NODE 130 BELOW 30 (Link 12 will be opened if the pressure at Node 130 drops below 30 psi); LINK PUMP02 1.5 AT TIME 16 (The relative speed of pump PUMP02 is set to 1.5 at 16 hours into the simulation); LINK 12 CLOSED AT CLOCKTIME 10 AM LINK 12 OPEN AT CLOCKTIME 8 PM (Two rules: Link 12 is repeatedly closed at 10 am and opened at 8 pm throughout the simulation)
keys.lpn_library_rules_tip: A rule opens or closes a link, or changes its setting, when a water level, a pressure, a flow, or the time reaches a set value. A rule can test more than one condition and can specify the action to take when the condition is false.
keys.lpn_library_rule_tip: One clause per line. Descriptions with examples in "ALL CAPS" follow. Line 1: Name of rule, "RULE 1". Line 2: A condition, "IF TANK 2 LEVEL BELOW 17.1". Line 3: An action, "THEN PUMP 9 STATUS IS OPEN". Line 4: A priority, "PRIORITY 1". Add "AND" or "OR" lines to test more than one condition, and "ELSE" lines to specify the action when the condition is false. A condition can read LEVEL, HEAD, GRADE, PRESSURE or DEMAND on a node, FLOW, STATUS or SETTING on a link, or TIME and CLOCKTIME on SYSTEM. Use consistent project units. Keywords must be in English.
keys.lpn_library_rule_bad: ⚠ This rule could not be read
keys.lpn_result_demand_tip: The flow this node draws at the time step shown: each base demand multiplied by its own pattern, added together. It is a result, not an input.
keys.lpn_field_head_pattern_tip: Pattern of this reservoir’s water level through the run. The head above is multiplied by the pattern.
keys.lpn_field_pump_speed_tip: Relative to the rotational speed used to generate its published performance curve. Ignored (not scaled) if there is a speed pattern.
keys.lpn_field_speed_pattern_tip: Each pattern entry gives the relative speed for that part of the run rather than scaling a base value.
keys.lpn_search_menu: Search for a place by name…
keys.lpn_search_tip: Permission is requested at first use, because searches are sent to the OpenStreetMap place-name service.
keys.lpn_search_consent_1: Search by place name sends the words you enter to nominatim.openstreetmap.org, the OpenStreetMap Foundation’s free place-name service.
keys.lpn_search_consent_2: This is a different service from the street map pictures behind your project. The pictures only say where you are looking. A search says what you entered. The place-name service will receive your search words and your IP address. We send nothing else, and we keep no record of your searches.
keys.lpn_search_consent_3: May we send your searches to the place-name service?
keys.lpn_search_consent_4: If you say no, everything else on this page keeps working exactly as it does now, including Go to a latitude and longitude. We remember a yes so that we need not ask again. A no is not stored at all.
keys.lpn_search_refused: Place-name search is off, and nothing was sent. The Go to a latitude and longitude command still works.
keys.lpn_search_prompt: Search for a place by name. A town, a street, a landmark — for example: Petaluma, California
keys.lpn_search_empty: Enter a place name to search for.
keys.lpn_search_busy: A search is already running. Wait for it to finish.
keys.lpn_search_choose: More than one place matches. Which one?
keys.lpn_search_nochoice: Nothing chosen, so the map has not moved.
keys.lpn_search_badchoice: That is not one of the numbers in the list.
keys.lpn_search_rate: The place-name service has limited the request rate. Wait a minute and try again.
keys.lpn_search_http: The place-name service returned an error.
keys.lpn_search_timeout: The place-name service did not respond in time. Everything else on this page works without it.
keys.lpn_search_unreadable: The place-name service returned a response this page could not read.
keys.lpn_search_offline: We could not reach the place-name service. You may be offline. Everything else on this page works without it, including Go to a latitude and longitude.
keys.lpn_search_toofast: The place-name service allows one search per second. Try again in a moment.
keys.lpn_search_nofetch: This browser cannot reach the place-name service.
keys.lpn_terrain_accuracy: Mapbox assembles this from many public elevation datasets, so its accuracy depends on location. Where a national lidar survey exists, such as USGS 3DEP in much of the United States and its equivalents elsewhere, it can be better than 1 m horizontally and a few tenths of a meter vertically. Where only global data exists, it is about 30 m horizontally and several meters vertically. Mapbox does not report which source applies. Treat it as a contour map, not a survey, and verify any value the design depends on.
keys.lpn_terrain_consent_1: Filling in elevations sends the position of each node that needs one — its latitude and longitude — to api.mapbox.com, to look up the height of the ground there.
keys.lpn_terrain_consent_2: This is a different question from the map pictures behind your project. The pictures only say where you are looking. These positions are your network itself. Mapbox will receive those coordinates and your IP address. We send nothing else: no name, no pipes, no project. We keep no record of it, and nothing is stored on this device except your answer to this question.
keys.lpn_terrain_consent_3: May we send your node positions to Mapbox?
keys.lpn_terrain_consent_4: If you say no, everything else on this page keeps working exactly as it does now, and elevations can be entered by hand as before. We remember a yes so that we need not ask again. A no is not stored at all.
keys.lpn_terrain_refused: Elevations were not filled in, and nothing was sent. They can be entered by hand as before.
keys.lpn_terrain_confirm: Fill in the elevation of {n} node(s) from Mapbox DEM?
keys.lpn_terrain_confirm_default_1: Every node already has an elevation, and {n} of them are still at {v}, which is the elevation a new node starts with rather than one you entered.
keys.lpn_terrain_confirm_default_2: Replace the elevation of those nodes ({n}) with values from the Mapbox DEM?
keys.lpn_terrain_keep: {k} node(s) already have an elevation and will not be changed.
keys.lpn_terrain_undo: One Undo (Ctrl-Z) puts every one of them back.
keys.lpn_terrain_busy: Elevations are already being filled in. Wait for that to finish.
keys.lpn_terrain_offmap: These node positions are not on the terrain map, so nothing was sent.
keys.lpn_terrain_too_wide: These nodes span too much of the Earth to read in one operation ({n} tile requests). Nothing was sent.
keys.lpn_terrain_cancelled: Nothing was changed and nothing was sent.
keys.lpn_terrain_nofetch: This browser cannot reach the terrain service.
keys.lpn_terrain_denied: The terrain service refused the request ({status}), so no elevation was changed. The Mapbox token this site uses may not allow the web address you are on.
keys.lpn_terrain_failed: We could not reach the terrain service, so no elevation was changed. You may be offline. Everything else on this page works without it.
keys.lpn_terrain_rate_limited: The terrain service has limited the request rate (429), so no elevation was changed. Try again in a minute.
keys.lpn_terrain_http: The terrain service answered with an error ({status}), so no elevation was changed. Nothing is wrong with your network.
keys.lpn_terrain_no_place: None of those nodes has a position on the Earth, so nothing was sent and no elevation was changed. Reading the land surface needs a project in latitude and longitude, or one on a projection this page can place.

keys.lpn_ff_menu_tip: Test each selected junction for fire flow, and check the effect on the rest of the system
keys.lpn_ff_intro:
Each junction in turn draws a fire flow on top of its existing demand. The run uses a copy of the network at the time step on screen, so nothing in the project is changed.

When the project has an extended-period simulation, Reporting step tested selects the condition: the time step on screen, a chosen reporting step, the reporting step of lowest pressure among the junctions tested, or every reporting step. The last option runs the sweep at each reporting step with the tank levels, demand patterns, and link statuses of that step, and shows each junction at its own worst step, the step with the lowest available flow, in the Step of lowest flow column.

Fire flow is normally tested at maximum day demand, so set the network to that condition first.

Each junction tested takes about 16 solves of the whole network, so a large system takes minutes: choose the junctions before you run, and stop at any time to keep the partial results.

The system counts as recovered when, at the last reporting step, no junction is more than about 0.14 psi (1 kPa) and no tank more than about 0.3 ft (0.1 m) from the run without the fire.

keys.lpn_crit_intro: Each asset is taken out of the network in turn, and the network is solved at the time step on screen in the active scenario. Nothing in the project is changed; the whole run is made on a copy.\n\nWhen the project has an extended-period simulation, Reporting step tested can be set to The whole run. Each outage is then simulated over the full run, and the table reports the lowest pressure and the reporting step at which it occurs, the hours any junction spends below the lowest pressure allowed, the reporting step at which a tank first empties, and the largest demand not served over the run. Lowest pressures are read only before a tank empties.

keys.lpn_ds_menu_tip: Multiply the demands on a copy of the network and see the pressures and velocities, or find the largest demand scale the system can carry.
keys.lpn_ds_intro:
Press the Run button to multiply the demands at the chosen junctions by the demand scale and see the pressures and velocities.

Press the Find button to find the largest demand scale, to the nearest {step}, at which all these junctions keep at least the lowest pressure allowed; it searches from 0 to {max}.

Both work on a copy of the network, solved at the time step on screen in the active scenario, so nothing in your project is changed. By default only the time step on screen is scaled, and levels and statuses are taken from it. When the project has an extended-period simulation, set Reporting step tested to The whole run to scale the demands over the entire run: every reporting step is judged, a tank that empties fails the scale, and the answer names the limiting reporting step.

keys.lpn_survey_err_ambiguous_coord: More than one column in that file could be the {axis} ({detail}), and this page does not choose between them. Leave only one of them named as the {axis} and try again.
keys.lpn_survey_err_no_points: Not one row of that file could be read as a surveyed point. Rows read: {detail}
keys.lpn_survey_note_header_unread: The first line was skipped: it names no columns this page knows.
keys.lpn_survey_report_clean: Every point in the file was imported without change.
keys.lpn_survey_note_row_short: Too few columns for the file format above.
keys.lpn_survey_note_bad_coord: The {axis} does not read as a number.
keys.lpn_survey_note_coord_range: The {axis} is outside the range this project allows.
keys.lpn_survey_note_ambiguous_elev: More than one column could be the elevation, so none of them was read.
keys.lpn_survey_note_id_duplicate: Name already used earlier in this file, new name assigned.
keys.lpn_survey_note_id_taken: Name already in project, new name assigned.
keys.lpn_survey_note_id_invalid: Name cannot be used here, new name assigned.
keys.lpn_survey_codes_toggle: Read the description as field codes
keys.lpn_survey_codes_tip: Read the first word of each description as a code from the table. Points with the same line code join into one pipe in file order, and WL1 and WL2 are separate lines. +0 starts a line, -0 ends one, and CLO closes one. JPN followed by a point name joins to that point (Carlson), and Civil 3D writes it CPN.
keys.lpn_survey_confirm_coded: {j} junction(s), {r} reservoir(s), {t} tank(s), and {p} pipe(s) found. Proceed?
keys.lpn_survey_report_coded: {j} junction(s), {r} reservoir(s), {t} tank(s), and {p} pipe(s) imported, {m} of the nodes with elevation.
keys.lpn_survey_note_code_unknown: Code not in the code table, imported as the asset type chosen above.
keys.lpn_survey_note_code_two_nodes: More than one node code, the first was used.
keys.lpn_survey_note_code_unread: Not every word is a code this page reads, kept in the description.
keys.lpn_survey_note_vertex_text: Not every word is a code this page reads, and a vertex keeps no description.
keys.lpn_survey_note_join_missing: JPN or CPN names a point not in this file or project, no pipe drawn for it.
keys.lpn_survey_note_join_no_line: JPN or CPN on a point with no line code, no pipe drawn for it.
keys.lpn_survey_note_pipe_one_node: This line returns to the same node with no other node between, no pipe drawn for it.
keys.lpn_survey_note_line_one_point: Only point on its line, no pipe drawn from it.
keys.lpn_survey_note_vertices: Points that became pipe vertices: {detail}. A vertex keeps no name, elevation, or description.
keys.lpn_survey_note_no_desc: Field codes are on, but this file has no description column, so no codes were read.
keys.lpn_survey_note_ring_junction: This point became a junction so the ring could close.
keys.lpn_survey_note_pipe_zero_length: This point is at the same spot as the node before it, so the pipe between them has no length.
keys.lpn_survey_note_node_on_pipe: This point lies exactly on a pipe it is not joined to. If they connect, add JPN to say so.
keys.lpn_settings_demand_model_tip: Choose how junctions receive flow. Demand driven (DDA) delivers every demand in full, whatever the pressure. Pressure driven (PDA) delivers less than the demand where the pressure is below the required pressure, and only the EPANET solver computes it.
keys.lpn_settings_min_pressure_tip: Enter the pressure at or below which a junction receives no flow. Use this project's pressure unit.
keys.lpn_settings_req_pressure_tip: Enter the pressure at or above which a junction receives its full demand. It must be greater than the minimum pressure. Use this project's pressure unit. Leave it blank to use EPANET's default, which is in psi for US flow units and meters otherwise.
keys.lpn_settings_pressure_exponent_tip: Enter the exponent of the curve that rises from no flow at the minimum pressure to the full demand at the required pressure.
keys.lpn_engine_pda_route: Solved with the EPANET solver, because the demand model is pressure driven.
keys.lpn_diag_valve_conflict: These control valves are joined to each other in a way EPANET does not allow, such as two pressure reducing valves in series. Insert a short pipe between them:
keys.lpn_diag_gpv_curve_order: The head loss curves of these general purpose valves cannot be read: each flow must be greater than the one before it, and a curve with one point needs a flow above zero:
keys.lpn_gpv_one_point_note: ⚠ These general purpose valves have a head loss curve with only one point, so their head loss was taken as proportional to flow, through that point: {ids}
keys.lpn_diag_pda_needs_epanet: The demand model is pressure driven, and only the EPANET solver can compute it. The EPANET solver could not be loaded, so these results are missing.
keys.lpn_result_delivered_demand_tip: The flow this junction actually receives under the pressure driven demand model. It is less than the demand when the pressure is below the required pressure.
keys.lpn_result_demand_deficit_tip: The demand at this junction that is not delivered, because the pressure is below the required pressure.
keys.lpn_pda_deficit_note: Junctions receiving less than their demand: {n}.
keys.lpn_diag_pda_pressures: Required pressure must be greater than Minimum pressure. Change one of them in Settings.
keys.lpn_inp_drop_pressure_unit: This file states a pressure unit other than the one this page reads for its flow unit, which is psi for US units and meters otherwise. Every pressure in the file is read that way, so check the valve settings, emitters, and pressure driven limits it holds. The line is kept and is written back.
keys.lpn_screenshot_tip: Take a picture of the map area you drag, at a higher resolution than the screen. Annotate it, then copy it into a report with the Copy button. Click without dragging to take the whole map.
keys.lpn_screenshot_hint: Drag a rectangle over the map, or click for the whole map. Esc cancels.
keys.lpn_screenshot_saved: The clipboard is not available here, so the screenshot was downloaded as a PNG file.
keys.lpn_screenshot_no_basemap: The street map or satellite image could not be included.
keys.lpn_screenshot_failed: The screenshot could not be made.
keys.lpn_snip_hint_free: Drag around the area to snip, or click for the whole map. Esc cancels.
keys.lpn_snip_tip_eraser: Eraser: click a stroke to remove it (E)
keys.lpn_screenshot_scale_tip: The picture's size as a multiple of the area on the screen. A larger one is sharper and makes a bigger file.
keys.lpn_export_holds_base: It holds the Base scenario only.
keys.lpn_geojson_results_other: No results are included, because the results on screen belong to the scenario {scenario}.
keys.lpn_survey_added_scenario: The nodes were added to {scenario}. In Base they are inactive.
keys.lpn_pane_pasted_scenario: These values are overrides in the scenario {scenario}.
keys.lpn_export_leaves_alternatives: The alternatives stored in this project are not in the file.
